analysis.one_liner: Maruti Suzuki is India's largest passenger car maker, selling small and mid-size cars domestically and through exports, with its parent Suzuki Motor Corporation also using India as a manufacturing and export hub.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter to Sept 2026) were announced on 27 Oct 2026: the company posted its highest-ever quarterly volume of 696,654 units (+26.5% YoY) and domestic market share rose 2.2 points to 40.8%, but consolidated net profit fell 26.4% YoY to ₹2,466 crore (standalone PAT down 27% to ₹2,415 crore) even as revenue grew 26% to ₹53,356 crore. Management flagged rising commodity costs - linked partly to the West Asia conflict - and mark-to-market losses on treasury investments as the drag on profit, despite EBITDA margin holding up better than feared at 8.9%.
analysis.plain_terms: Maruti is selling more cars than it ever has, but making less profit per car - that is the central tension. A GST cut on small cars (28% to 18%, effective Sept 2025) plus heavy festive discounting pulled in record volumes, but rising input costs and mark-to-market losses on investments pulled profit down for a third straight quarter. The company has already raised prices three times this year and is now waiting to see if raw material costs settle. None of this involves a stock split or spin-off - it is a straightforward margin story, not an accounting artefact.
analysis.quarters: The margin trend has been deteriorating for three quarters straight. Q4 FY26 (to Mar 2026): PAT fell 6.9% YoY to ₹3,590 crore, EBITDA margin 11.7%. Q1 FY27 (to Jun 2026): PAT fell 10.8% YoY to ₹3,352 crore as EBITDA margin contracted ~400bps to 8.6%, with material costs rising from 76.7% to 80.5% of sales. Q2 FY27 (to Sep 2026): standalone PAT fell 27% YoY to ₹2,415 crore (consolidated -26.4% to ₹2,466 crore); EBITDA margin ticked up slightly to 8.9% but operating profit still fell 17.1% YoY. CFO Arnab Roy said the company has raised prices in three tranches and is watching whether commodity costs stabilise after recent geopolitical developments. Guidance for H2 FY27: at least 10% domestic sales growth, 7-10% overall volume growth with exports roughly flat; pending customer orders stood near 270,000 units by Dussehra, pointing to strong underlying demand.
analysis.performance_read: There are no splits or corporate actions in this stock's history, so the raw price series is a clean read with no adjustment needed. The stock is down 33.4% from its January 2026 peak of ₹17,120 to ₹11,397, close to its 52-week low of ₹11,170. Over 1 year it is down 29% versus Nifty's -11% and peer M&M's -18% - a sharp underperformance tied to the margin miss. More striking is the longer run: 3-year return of just 13% and 5-year return of 57% both badly lag the Nifty (21% and 29%) and especially M&M (100% and 242%) - Maruti has been a long-term laggard against both the index and its key peer, not just a recent casualty.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 27x, Maruti trades in line with the peer median, so the 33% price fall has not made it statistically cheap - consensus earnings have been cut alongside the price as margins compressed. P/B of 3.3x is about 5% below the peer median of 3.48x, a modest discount. The 'why' here is earnings downgrades following margin compression, not an unrecognised bargain: ROE of 14.3% trails the peer median of around 22%, so paying a market-average multiple for below-peer returns on equity is not obviously inexpensive.
analysis.growth_read: This is volume-led growth, not margin-led. Units sold rose 26.5% YoY and market share expanded, helped by the September 2025 GST cut on small cars and heavy festive-season discounting (festive retail sales up ~90% YoY). But EBITDA margin has fallen in three successive quarters (11.7% to 8.6% to 8.9%), meaning volume gains have not translated into proportionate profit growth - a less durable pattern than if both volume and margin were rising together.
analysis.health_read: The balance sheet is effectively debt-free (total debt is a trivial ~₹100 crore) and operating cash flow was roughly ₹19,100 crore in FY26, comfortably funding free cash flow of about ₹8,977 crore - profits are backed by real cash generation. The risk here is business/margin risk - commodity costs and competitive pricing in the small-car segment - not financial or leverage risk.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter Suzuki Motor Corporation holds 56.28% of a total promoter stake of 58.7%, unchanged for four straight quarters, with 0% pledging. Foreign institutional investors have trimmed their holding to 12.4% from 15.8% a year earlier, while domestic institutions increased their stake to 25.4% from 22.9% - a notable rotation from foreign to domestic ownership. No specific marquee individual investor was found on the register in available data.
strengths: Record quarterly volume of 696,654 units (+26.5% YoY) with domestic market share up 2.2 points to 40.8%
Virtually debt-free balance sheet (total debt ~₹100 crore) against FY26 operating cash flow of ~₹19,100 crore
ROCE of roughly 19%, above the peer benchmark of ~16.3%
Zero promoter pledging, with promoter stake stable at 58.7% for four consecutive quarters
watchpoints: Net profit has declined for three consecutive quarters (Q4 FY26 -6.9%, Q1 FY27 -10.8%, Q2 FY27 standalone -27%) on rising commodity costs
EBITDA margin has fallen from 11.7% (Q4 FY26) to the 8.6-8.9% range through FY27 so far
ROE of 14.3% trails the peer median of ~22%, and FIIs have cut their holding from 15.8% to 12.4% over the past year
Stock is down ~33% from its January 2026 peak and has underperformed both Nifty and peer M&M over 1, 3 and 5 years
analysis.one_thing: Whether EBITDA margin climbs back above the 11%+ levels seen before FY27 as management's three rounds of price hikes catch up with commodity costs - that single number will show whether record volumes are finally converting back into profit growth.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 profit decline (~26-27%) and EBITDA margin (~8.9%) were cross-checked across multiple independent sources (IANS, just-auto, Kotak Neo, GuruFocus earnings-call summary) and were consistent. Shareholding and pledge figures were cross-checked via Trendlyne/MarketsMojo-type summaries. The exact net cash balance could not be reliably verified - sources gave inconsistent crore/million figures - so treat any specific cash balance as 'Not verified - check on Screener'; the near-zero total debt figure and FY26 operating/free cash flow figures were internally consistent and used with more confidence.
